topic: The Monthly Twenty: a calm 20-minute Sunday reset to look at your Three Numbers again and pick one small step
pillar: THE MONTHLY TWENTY: a gentle weekly or monthly reset, looking at your three numbers again, one small step.
caption:
Sunday is a good day to look, not judge. ☕
Set a timer for twenty minutes.
Check your Three Numbers again: what came in, what went out, how many months you could keep going.
Then pick one small step from Keep, Cut, Earn or Build. Just one.
Save this so it is here next Sunday.
If you want a place to track it month to month, the Day Zero Workbook is in my Stan store, link in bio.
Day one counts.

General education, not financial advice.

#lifeafterdivorce #moneyreset #sundayreset #startingover #budgetingforbeginners

slides.title: Your Sunday money reset, in twenty minutes
slides.subtitle: Three numbers. One small step.

slides.title: A check-in you can finish
slides.body: Once a month, or once a week if that feels better, you sit down for twenty minutes. You look at your numbers, notice what changed, and pick one small thing. That is the whole job.

slides.title: Set it up in two minutes
items: Set a timer for twenty minutes.
Grab your phone or laptop and last month's notes.
Open your bank app and any card apps.
Make tea or coffee. This is allowed to be nice.

slides.title: Look at your Three Numbers again
items: How many months could you keep going?
Write each one down. Rough is fine.

slides.title: What it can look like
slides.body: Say 3,000 came in, 2,800 went out, and you have 1,400 set aside. That is about half a month of going. It is simply where you are today.

slides.title: Then pick just one step
items: Keep: name one thing that is worth it to protect.
Cut: cancel one charge you forgot about.
Earn: jot down one idea, no pressure to act.
Build: add one line to your plan for next month.

slides.title: Then close the laptop
slides.body: Write today's date and your one step on a sticky note. Then stop. Twenty minutes is enough. You can come back next month, or next Sunday.

slides.title: Save this for your next reset
slides.body: If you want one place to keep your numbers each month, the Day Zero Workbook has pages for it. It is a 32-page guide in my Stan store, link in bio. Day one counts.
